subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 31-year-old woman and her unrelated 33-year-old husband seek genetic counseling after their first child died at age 3 years of a progressive demyelinating disorder. Postmortem studies showed diffuse loss of myelin with metachromatic granules within oligodendrocytes and peripheral nerves, and arylsulfatase A activity was absent in the child's leukocytes. Both parents are asymptomatic and have no affected relatives.
question: Which of the following is the risk that their next child will be affected by the same disorder?
explanation_correct: Metachromatic leukodystrophy is an autosomal recessive deficiency of arylsulfatase A, so both asymptomatic parents of an affected child must be obligatory carriers. With each pregnancy, an autosomal recessive couple has a 25% chance of an affected child, a 50% chance of an unaffected carrier, and a 25% chance of a noncarrier. This is why sphingolipidoses, including metachromatic leukodystrophy, are classified among the autosomal recessive diseases.

explanation_incorrect.A: A 100% risk would require both parents to be homozygous affected, which is not the case because both are asymptomatic.
explanation_incorrect.B: A 50% risk per pregnancy applies to autosomal dominant disease or to a carrier of an X-linked recessive allele having an affected son.
explanation_incorrect.C: Sex does not alter the risk in an autosomal disorder; male and female children are affected with equal frequency.
explanation_incorrect.D: The risk is not negligible because both parents are obligatory carriers of the same autosomal recessive mutation.

educationalObjective: Two asymptomatic parents of a child with an autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder have a 25% recurrence risk in each subsequent pregnancy.
